posts.title: The Eight-Sided Pyramid
posts.hook: The Great Pyramid actually has eight sides
posts.narration: The Great Pyramid actually has eight sides. Each of its four main faces is slightly concave. This makes a very slight dip in the center. You can see this from the air. During the spring and autumn equinoxes, the sun hits the pyramid. The low sun puts half of a face in shadow. Follow us to learn more secrets.
posts.caption:
Did you know the Great Pyramid actually has eight sides?

It turns out each face is slightly curved inward. You can see this from the sky. A British Air Force pilot named P. Groves actually captured the first photo of it back in 1940. This is visible during the spring and autumn equinoxes when the low sun casts a shadow over half of a face. 😮

Do you think the builders did this on purpose or was it just an accident?

posts.fact: The Great Pyramid of Giza has eight sides due to its slightly concave faces, which are visible from the air during the spring and autumn equinoxes.

posts.title: Why Reindeer Eyes Turn Blue in Winter
posts.hook: Reindeer change their eye color every winter
posts.narration: Reindeer change their eye color every winter. In summer, their eyes are warm golden brown. When polar darkness hits, they turn deep blue, acting like built-in night vision. The constant dark increases pressure inside the eye, squeezing a tissue layer behind the retina to reflect blue light. That simple shift helps improve their vision in the dark. Follow along for more wild animal facts.
posts.caption:
I just found out reindeer change their eye color to see in the winter.

During the summer, a reindeer has golden brown eyes. But when winter brings constant polar darkness, pressure inside their eyes builds up. This extra pressure compresses a reflective tissue layer behind the retina, changing how light bounces off it and turning their eyes deep blue. Reflecting blue light helps improve their night vision in the dark.

Would you choose blue night vision if you had to live in total darkness? 🦌

#reindeer #arcticwildlife #reindeereyes #polarwinter #animaladaptations #aigenerated
posts.fact: Reindeer eyes change color from golden brown in the summer to deep blue in the winter to improve their vision in constant polar darkness.
